lines: {maker} found this {form} humming on a hillside near {place}. Nobody has explained the {word} pattern inside it yet.
Carry it anywhere near {place} and it hums like a kettle about to boil. Nobody knows why, but the kettles there are excellent.
On clear nights it glows like a lamp-tower in miniature. The children of {place} call it a pocket star.
{maker} of {place} worked this {form} for three winters and signed it where only another maker would look.
A {culture} {form}, made the slow way. The {word} pattern worked into it was put there on purpose.
Apprentices in {place} still copy this {form}. None of them has got the {word} quite right.
Passed from aunt to niece in {place} for six generations, and never lost for long.
{maker} made this {form} as half of a pair. The other half is still somewhere near {place}.
{faction} lend this {form} to whoever keeps the hearth that winter.
Carried at the head of every festival parade in {place}, and dropped in the river at least once a year.
This {form} opened the first harvest feast at {place}. It still smells faintly of {word} and honey cake.
{faction} award this {form} to the year's best dancer. {maker} won it four times and mentions it often.
{maker} carried this {form} from {place} to the edge of the map, and came home with a new dent to prove it.
Every scratch on this {form} is a road. The newest one points past {place}.
A wayfarer's {form}. It leans toward {place} whenever its owner is about to get lost.
Dug out of a fallen lamp-tower near {place}, still warm. Nobody at the Ledger recognizes the hand that made it.
The {form} that showed {maker} the way into the old vaults beneath {place}.
Scholars of {faction} have argued about this {form} for forty years. The {word} on its side might be a glyph.
{maker} made this {form} to beat a rival from {place}. The rival made a better one. They got married.
Prize of the yearly race at {place}. {faction} have won it nine times and bring it up often.
Made to settle a bet between two {culture} makers. Both sides say this {form} proves them right.
Made in the Lamplit Age by a {culture} smith whose name has worn off, and still in daily use at {place}.
Said to have belonged to someone who knew {legend}. {faction} keep a careful copy, just in case.
{maker} left this {form} to {place} with a note: for whoever needs it next.
This {form} warms in the hand as you walk toward {place}, where it was made.
{maker} carried this {form} for twenty years abroad. It was the first thing unpacked in {place}.
It hung by the door in {place}, and every traveler touched it on the way back in.
{maker} made this {form} for someone who did not come home to {place}. It was kept polished anyway.
Found in a waycairn on the road past {place}, with a faded ribbon still tied around it.
The last thing {maker} mended before the Hush emptied {place}. The stitching is still good.
Carried at the Silent Field by a Concord scribe, who scratched a {word} pattern along its edge for luck.
Pulled from a broken Imperative construct near {place}. It still tries to give orders.
A {culture} {form} from the Quarrel, mended many times since. Whoever owned it wanted it to last.
{maker} was sent away from {place} with nothing but this {form}, and made it go a long way.
Its {culture} make is unmistakable, yet it turned up very far from {place}. Somebody walked a long road.
{faction} closed their doors to {maker}. This {form} is how the craft survived anyway.
Nobody in {place} will touch this {form} after dark. It has never actually done anything. Yet.
A sliver of the Iron Sentence is set into it. It works very well, and it likes being obeyed.
{maker} wrote one word too many on this {form}. The {word} never quite settles.
